Hi Alice,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the connector looks promising for the marketplace offer. Before we progress to a pilot I need a clear mapping of how customer telemetry flows when the connector is used in a Redwood Private deployment. We have a few compliance gates to clear for EU customers and need the information in the attached matrix. Can you confirm the following items on your side and return an annotated copy?

- Which Datadog services see customer payloads (Traces, Metrics, Logs) and where those services store data at rest by region (EU/US/APAC).
- Whether Datadog holds any unredacted customer PII in logs or traces by default; if so, the retention controls available.
- In-transit encryption specifics: TLS version, mutual TLS support, and whether traffic can be routed over PrivateLink/VPC peering instead of public endpoints.
- How sampling decisions are made in the connector vs agent-side sampling; deterministic sampling guarantees for downstream rehydration (important for root-cause reproducibility).
- Key management: do you recommend customer-managed keys (CMK) for data at rest in the EU region? If yes, is that available for the connector offer?

I attached a baseline dataflow matrix and our current connector architecture diagram. If you can annotate the matrix and call out any contractual/technical gaps we should expect, that will be most helpful.

Can we target a follow-up call next Tue 4/13 at 10am BST (3am PT) to walk through your annotations? If that time doesn't work, propose alternatives.

Thanks,

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear list and the matrix. Quick summary answers up front, detailed annotations attached.

- Storage by service/region: Traces/Logs/Custom Metrics are stored in the region where the ingestion endpoint receives them. For our managed SaaS, EU customers' data can be pinned to EU clusters (Frankfurt/Paris) under our EU data residency program; however some backend metadata (routing metadata) may be processed in a multi-region control plane. See matrix row A2 for specifics.
- PII in payloads: Datadog does not automatically redact payload fields. We provide processors and rules to strip fields at ingestion; customers can configure processors in the connector pipeline. Retention is configurable per-organization; default is 30 days for logs, 90 days for traces (can be extended under contract).
- In-transit encryption: TLS 1.2+ supported; we also support mutual TLS for private peering (mTLS). PrivateLink is supported for AWS, and a VPC peering + NAT option for GCP/Azure. Public endpoints are TLS only.
- Sampling behavior: by default the connector forwards sampling headers and honors upstream sampling decisions. Deterministic sampling for reconciling replays requires turning on the "preserve-sampling" mode; this stores sampling metadata in a side-channel and requires longer retention for the sampling keys (see note in matrix B4).
- KMS/CMK: Customer-managed keys are supported for EU storage under our enterprise offering; we'd need a DPA addendum and a EKMS configuration during onboarding.

I've attached an annotated copy of your matrix and an internal DPA draft (confidential). I'm looping in Datadog Security (security@datadog.com) for the contractual bits.

Best,
Alice
Principal Partner Engineer — Integrations, Datadog
Attachments: annotated-dataflow-matrix.xlsx, datadog-dpa-draft-annotated.pdf

Hello Laura / Kimberly,

Quick note from Datadog Security on the asks below:

- Metadata fields leaving EU control plane: we typically see request IDs, route tags, and aggregated telemetry counters propagated for platform operations. Full trace payloads and log bodies remain in-region if EU pinning is requested. We'll provide a scoped exportable list by EOD Wed 4/14.
- CMK and key handling: when customers opt for CMK, Datadog performs envelope encryption; the customer retains CMK ownership in KMS. Datadog never stores plaintext key material. Rotation is initiated by the customer or on a schedule agreed in the onboarding docs; audit logs are available and can be surfaced to a customer tenant's audit export.
- Preserve-sampling side-channel: stored as encrypted metadata in our EU storage tier when EU pinning is enabled. Access is limited to platform services; customer audit logs will show access records. Retention matches whatever retention policy you set for traces, but if you request longer retention for sampling keys we can set that per contract.

We understand the legal ask for an explicit DPA amendment with EU storage guarantee and audit access for key rotation logs. Typical lead time for a DPA addendum is 3–4 weeks with our standard enterprise legal process. Happy to sync with Redwood Legal on a redline.

Regards,
Datadog Security Team
